questions.prompt: What is the single most effective way to reduce a page's JavaScript bundle?

options.text: Keep components as Server Components and isolate "use client" to small leaves
Inline every third-party script in the head

questions.explanation: Server Components ship zero JavaScript. Keeping work on the server and isolating interactivity is the biggest bundle-size lever.

options.text: Code-splits a component so its JS loads on demand, with an optional placeholder
Converts a Server Component into a Route Handler

questions.explanation: next/dynamic dynamically imports (lazy-loads) a component so its code is fetched only when rendered, optionally showing a loading fallback.

questions.prompt: Which Core Web Vital measures loading — when the main content appears? Type its three-letter acronym.
questions.explanation: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) measures when the largest/main content becomes visible.

questions.prompt: Which are good performance practices in Next.js? Select all that apply.

options.text: Lazy-load heavy client code with next/dynamic
Use next/image and next/font to protect LCP and CLS
Load third-party scripts with next/script and a strategy
Mark every component "use client" to be safe

questions.explanation: Lazy-loading, image/font optimization, and next/script all help. Over-using "use client" bloats the bundle.

questions.prompt: Match each Core Web Vital to what it measures.
questions.explanation: LCP is loading, CLS is stability, INP is responsiveness; next/image helps LCP/CLS by optimizing images and reserving space.

items.text: Measure current Core Web Vitals and bundle size
Keep non-interactive components as Server Components
Lazy-load heavy client code with next/dynamic

questions.explanation: Measure first, cut client JS by favoring Server Components, defer heavy client code, then re-measure to verify the gains.
